Additionally, GoogleCalendarService's new fallbacks `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` are dead when externalCalendarId is undefined. So bookings created via credential-less destinations lose the stored externalCalendarId, breaking subsequent update/delete targeting the correct calendar — a real regression introduced by this diff.

judged_text: The reference mapping takes externalCalendarId from result.externalId, but createAllCalendarEvents' legacy branch calls createEvent(c, event) without passing destination.externalId, so references for credential-less destinations are now stored with no externalCalendarId (previously evt.destinationCalendar.externalId); the identical edit sits at lines 208-209. Bookings created through a destinationCalendar without credentialId become un-updatable and un-cancellable on the correct calendar: their stored reference has no externalCalendarId and GoogleCalendarService's update/delete fallbacks are dead code, so reschedule and cancel of those bookings fail.

adjudication.rationale: Diff shows EventManager now stores calendar references using `externalCalendarId: isCalendarType ? result.externalId : undefined` (replacing `evt.destinationCalendar?.externalId`). But `CalendarManager.createEvent` only returns `externalId` when its new 3rd param is provided. In `createAllCalendarEvents`, the legacy branch for destinations without `credentialId` calls `createEvent(c, event)` (no 3rd arg) while iterating `destinationCalendarCredentials`, so `result.externalId` will be `undefined` and the persisted reference will lack `externalCalendarId`. This is a behavior change compared to the old code path that derived the external calendar from `evt.destinationCalendar.externalId`, and it can break later update/delete flows that rely on `externalCalendarId` to target the correct calendar.
